title: russian air strikes injure two cause fire 9 storey apartment building kyiv 2026 09 11
text:
Sept 11 (Reuters) - At least two people were killed in a Ukrainian drone attack on ‌Russia's Tula region, while eight people were injured in Russian air strikes which caused a fire in a nine-storey apartment building in Kyiv on Friday morning, the authorities said.
Ukraine, which has been defending itself against Russia since February ​2022, says the strikes are part of a campaign to "bring the war home" to ordinary ​Russians and raise the cost to Moscow of continuing the conflict.
Both Russia and Ukraine ⁠deny targeting civilians.
Russia returned to its near-constant air attacks on Kyiv this week after a brief halt ​during the visit to Moscow and Kyiv of U.S. President Donald Trump's negotiators seeking to end the war ​which the Kremlin started by invading Ukraine in 2022.
Reuters footage showed servicemen trying to put out a fire at the apartment building in Kyiv where a number of windows were blown out.
In Russia, Tula region's governor Dmitry Milyayev said on ​Telegram that two people were killed and another three were injured in drone attacks overnight.
Ukrainian drones also damaged ​civilian infrastructure in the central Volga River city of Saratov, regional governor Roman Busargin said on Telegram, adding that ‌there ⁠were no casualties.
Russian e-commerce company Ozon said on Telegram that a Ukraine drone attack caused a fire at its logistics hub in Saratov, adding to more than two dozen warehouses, owned by Ozon and its top peer Wildberries, that have been recently hit.
The Saratov region, a frequent target of Ukrainian air strikes, including an ​attack earlier this week, ​is home to a ⁠large oil refinery run by state oil company Rosneft (ROSN.MM)
, opens new tab
, as well as a number of other industrial and military facilities.
In the city of Volgograd south ​of Saratov and also located on the Volga River, a missile attack ​injured two after ⁠hitting two residential buildings, with its debris also damaging an industrial facility, local authorities said on Telegram.
They said a temporary makeshift shelter was set up at a school for people from the damaged houses.
The post did not provide ⁠details about ​the industrial facility. The Volgograd oil refinery run by Lukoil (LKOH.MM)
, opens new tab
, ​one of Russia's biggest by processing capacity, is located on the outskirts of the city.
Reuters could not immediately verify the reports.
